prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Repaint this whole world-map concept as a sophisticated, restrained HAND-PAINTED GAME ATLAS. Preserve its exact wide 3:2 layout, all narrative places, paths, relationships and the distinct pine green / jade / muted rust-red palette. This is NOT a photorealistic scene or densely etched matte painting. The reference is much too detailed. Reduce detail dramatically: use large smooth color shapes with gently irregular painted edges and a few expressive ink contours. Replace forests with grouped masses and a few silhouette trees; rock walls with 3-4 broad tonal planes; roofs with simple dark shapes and at most 2-3 structural lines; water with a few clear painted strokes. Remove individual roof tiles, stone chips, tiny foliage, scratches, mottling, wood grain, noise, paper texture and repeated hatch patterns. A small handful of painterly accents per landmark, NOT evenly distributed tiny detail. Keep architecture and functional landmarks unmistakable at thumbnail scale, retain beautiful controlled light and spatial layering, don't make it childish, crude, cheap clip-art or flat monochrome. It should look like a beautifully authored navigation map made of about 80 thoughtfully painted large shapes, not a scenic illustration of thousands of objects. No text, letters, numbers, pins, badge UI or frame. Leave calm room around landmarks for selectable nodes. Keep ONE village gate, the ferry dock, distinct lower bier road and upper ridge, waterfall, hillside homes, storehouse with bier, two ritual courtyards and ONE red-cord ancient tree. Make the wooden bridge visibly broken with a gap in its center. Scale the upper-right ancient tree down slightly so its entire canopy fits within a generous top margin.
